transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-21 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Leah (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood Solutions), Priya (Aurora Nexus CTO), Daniel (Platform Eng), Rashid (Security)

Summary (auto): Align on perf gates for marketplace connector, clarify KMS/SAML flows for private deployment, agree on next steps for benchmark and UAT.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Leah Park: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 50 ish minutes. Marco and I will run through the connector performance plan and then hand off to Rashid for the security questions.
[00:14] Priya Menon: Yeah, thanks Leah. We wanted to make this explicit — our goals are marketplace listing but also an onprem/private deployment behind our VPC. So two tracks.
[00:26] Marco Silva: Perfect. Quick intro, I'm Marco, I'm the SE on the Redwood side. We'll be executing the benchmark and helping with tuning — batching, KV cache, and quantiz, uh quantization tradeoffs. Apologies, my voice is a bit rough.
[00:39] Daniel Cho: No worries. Quick context — our platform runs bursts up to 3k RPS for short windows, average is closer to 120 RPS. Sequence length usually 128 tokens but there are summary jobs at 1024 which matter for memory.
[00:55] Marco Silva: Good to note. That explains some of the p99 spikes we saw in the sample traces. For the Redwood connector we recommend a two-variant approach: hosted listing variant (lower mem, higher latency acceptable) and private-dedicated variant (reserved GPUs, p99 SLO).
[01:13] Rashid Ahmed: When you say private-dedicated, do you mean Redwood Dedicated or private with our KMS? We need to be clear on key custody.
[01:24] Marco Silva: Right — sorry, let me be specific. Options are: Redwood Hosted (Redwood api) — keys managed by Redwood; Redwood Dedicated — reserved capacity in our cloud with customer config options; Redwood Private — VPC/on-prem where customer manages KMS/HSM. In your case, you asked for customer KMS and audit logs, so Private fits best.
[01:42] Priya Menon: Ok, Private with HSM is preferred. But for marketplace listing we still need a hosted flavor.
[01:49] Leah Park: Yep, and we can list both variants. Marketplace listing metadata includes whether private connectors exist and a link to the connector repo/helm chart. That part is just a listing metadata field.
[02:05] Daniel Cho: Can you describe telemetry? We need to make sure we can pipe logs to our internal observability and not leak PII.
[02:13] Hannah Cortez: So telemetry from the connector is configurable — token-level telemetry is off by default, we emit anonymized metrics (throughput, latency histograms, error rates). For private deployments we provide an optional sidecar that forwards Prometheus metrics and structured traces. There is also an option to route logs to customer-owned ES/OTel collector.
[02:35] Rashid Ahmed: Good. For compliance, we need audit logs (who called what model, time, request id) and key rotation support. How does KMS integration look?
[02:45] Marco Silva: For Private, we have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS#11. We store only encrypted key handles, no raw keys in the control plane. There are a couple of mis-recognized product names in early docs — we'll send the canonical KMS flow doc.
[03:02] Priya Menon: And SSO? We have SAML enterprise SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.
[03:08] Leah Park: We support SAML SSO and SSO with OIDC; SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with granular route-level permissions. For marketplace listing you'll need to provide an admin contact and the RBAC mapping you expect.
[03:22] Daniel Cho: About performance: what perf gates do you recommend for listing? We don't want to fail customers but want to be honest about p99.
[03:30] Marco Silva: We usually publish median and p99 for a standard 512-token workload on the listing page. For the connector, we propose a pass criteria: median < 150ms per token and p99 under 2.5s for 512 tokens on the hosted variant — numbers tighter for Dedicated. But those numbers vary with quantization and batching.
[03:51] Priya Menon: That p99 seems optimistic for our 1k seq jobs.
[03:55] Marco Silva: Totally. For long sequences we recommend a second benchmark class. We'll run two bench profiles: short (avg 128 tokens) and long (avg 1024 tokens) and report both. The marketplace listing will show both so customers know tradeoffs.
[04:12] Hannah Cortez: Also want to flag caching — prefix/KV cache — using the K V cache can dramatically reduce cost for repeated contexts. But it affects freshness semantics so design matters.
[04:24] Daniel Cho: Do you have an SDK or sidecar for caching?
[04:27] Marco Silva: We provide a caching sidecar and SDK adapters for common runtimes. We'll include sample configs. There is a known issue where streaming plus KV cache interacts poorly with certain load balancer TCP timeouts — we'll note that in the docs.
[04:43] Rashid Ahmed: On the security front, we need to validate encryption-at-rest, in-transit, and auditability. Does Redwood provide FIPS-140 options for keys?
[04:53] Marco Silva: For Private deployments you can point to your HSM; that supports FIPS. Our Hosted and Dedicated default KMS is not FIPS by default, but we can provide options for enterprise plans. We'll share a matrix.
[05:06] Priya Menon: OK. For the bench plan, can you explain methodology? We need to know if you're using synthetic or replay workloads.
[05:12] Marco Silva: We'll run both. Step 1: replay a 24–48 hour window with your sanitized traces to replicate burst patterns. Step 2: synthetic steady-state runs at target QPS with varied seq lengths and token distributions. We'll measure throughput, latency histograms, GPU util, and memory. We'll also capture token-level cost approximations.
[05:32] Daniel Cho: Sanitation — we need to sanitize traces before sending. Is there a recommended toolchain?
[05:36] Marco Silva: We can provide a redaction script and an example dataset. Also we can run bench inside your VPC if you prefer so no data leaves your network — that's the private runner option.
[05:47] Priya Menon: That would be ideal.
[05:50] Leah Park: Great. Let's talk rollout — for canarying we suggest gradual traffic shifts with automatic fallback to the old provider if p99 or error rate thresholds are exceeded. Does Aurora have a feature-flagging system?
[06:00] Daniel Cho: We do, yes. Our infra team can do a canary with route-based splitting.
[06:05] Marco Silva: Perfect. We'll recommend canary policy: start at 5% for 24 hours, then 25% for 12 hours, then 50% etc, with automated rollback if errors exceed 0.5% or p99 > threshold.
[06:20] Rashid Ahmed: On logging — we need request-level audit that ties to our internal request id. Can you pass through our request id header?
[06:27] Hannah Cortez: Yes, headers can be forwarded and stored in audit logs. We also support masking of user content fields before logs are stored.
[06:35] Priya Menon: Any limitations with quantization on hallucination or accuracy drift? We want to be careful.
[06:41] Marco Silva: Quantization reduces model size but can affect accuracy slightly; we recommend our tested quant profiles per model family. We'll run a quality regression test against your eval prompts as part of the bench. If drift > X% we'll show options: higher precision or mixed precision.
[06:58] Daniel Cho: For the marketplace listing, what's required from our side?
[07:02] Leah Park: Minimal requirements: listing name, short description, the two variants you want listed, an admin contact, and a small metadata file (links to helm chart, preflight checklist). We'll send a template.
[07:12] Priya Menon: Good. Also want to discuss SLAs for Dedicated — is that already documented?
[07:18] Leah Park: Yes, Dedicated has SLA tiers. We'll attach the SLA doc. For Private deployments SLAs are negotiated — the platform is customer operated so Redwood provides the software support runbook.
[07:31] Rashid Ahmed: One more: incident response and root cause. We need clear runbooks and on-call contact.
[07:36] Marco Silva: We'll include an incident runbook and a communication plan. For Private we'll do an initial run with your ops team to test the playbook.
[07:46] Priya Menon: Ok, can we circle back to the bench scheduling? We want the bench to run next week.
[07:50] Marco Silva: We can start the sandbox bench on Monday. We'll need sanitized traces and an infra window for us to run the runner inside your VPC. Estimated time: 48 hours to complete runs and preliminary analysis within 72 hours of start.
[08:03] Daniel Cho: On the data retention side, logs retention must be configurable. Can we set 30 days retention for request logs and 90 days for metrics?
[08:11] Hannah Cortez: Yes, retention is configurable per tenant. We'll document retention policies and retention config options.
[08:20] Priya Menon: Anything else for marketplace listing compliance?
[08:23] Leah Park: We'll need a short privacy blurb and any compliance attestations (SOC2, ISO). We'll include our SOC2 summary and you can attach your addendum if needed.
[08:34] Rashid Ahmed: Please make sure the security pack includes the encryption cipher suites and TLS versions supported.
[08:39] Marco Silva: Noted. We'll also include our recommended hardening checklist for the helm chart.
[08:47] Priya Menon: Great. Quick note — for the bench, can you also measure cost per 1k tokens across variants?
[08:52] Marco Silva: Yes, cost per 1k tokens will be part of the output. We'll show estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private-runner overhead.
[09:01] Leah Park: Ok let's recap. Action items: Marco runs bench, Leah sends security pack & listing template, Daniel and Priya to provide sanitized traces and schedule UAT. We aim to meet next week to review.
[09:14] Priya Menon: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[09:18] Daniel Cho: Only procurement signoff for privilege access to infra runner, but we can do that fast.
[09:22] Rashid Ahmed: I'll prepare a list of required compliance artifacts.
[09:25] Marco Silva: I'll post the bench plan and a sample grafana dashboard link after this call.
[09:30] Leah Park: I'll create the follow-up invite for Thursday to review results. Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Priya Menon: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
